Factory/release signing should prefer offline or HSM/KeyVM-held keys over convenience file-key copies.

Factory and regulated deployments should treat receipted replication plus recurring restore drills as the default recovery story.

Factory/production maintenance access should be maintenance-window-shaped, JIT certificate based, and stronger-approved rather than standing.
Factory/regulatory operations should support bounded offline time bootstrap via signed/operator time or authenticated quorum rather than internet-dependent emergency waiver.

Production/manufacturing trust bundles on D should be fixed-purpose, digest-bound, and offline/strongly-approved; ad-hoc live CA edits are not the production trust story.
Factory/regulatory destructive reprovision on D should use offline signed reset authority plus a physical or attended-station reset signal rather than ad-hoc live rescue wipes.
Factory/regulatory cleanup must preserve approved rollback and audit windows and stay maintenance/offline/receipted rather than ad-hoc live cleanup folklore.

Factory/regulatory fuzz posture on D keeps approved production target sets explicit, retains corpora/crash artifacts longer, and treats open production-relevant reproducible cases as release blockers by default.

fleet_host.label: A) Secure fleet host
notes: Prefer Linux compatibility via Linux-in-microVM adapters rather than syscall translation.
Hostname-based allowlists must be broker-resolved/evidenced rather than delegated to ambient local resolver behavior.
Loopback-only debug is easy; broader service exposure belongs to brokered service classes rather than ad-hoc host firewall edits.
Remote assistance on fleet hosts is an operator-session lane; do not grow a general GUI remote-control story on the host.
Operator or workload key use should be brokered by policy; do not normalize host-local file-key sprawl.
Human operator accounts may exist for break-glass or maintenance, but portable homes are not the fleet-host default.
Fleet hosts are replaceable; back up state datasets via receipted replication and rehearse restore rather than treating full-host image backups as the primary recovery model.
Mutable host state should be encrypted by default; unattended unlock belongs to attested local or brokered recovery lanes rather than static file-key convenience.
External evidence handoff should be ticket-shaped and encrypted by default; boundary expansion belongs in review/gate lanes rather than incident shell folklore.
Operator access should use brokered short-lived certs and role shells by default; escalation stays separate from login.
Fleet hosts should treat secure time as a governed dependency: authenticated sources + LKGT + explicit degraded receipts rather than silent NTP fallback during incidents.
Measured platform posture should be receipted and ready to gate sensitive admissions (identity issuance, secret release, rollout) rather than living as raw quote folklore.
Fleet services should prefer digest-bound short-lived workload identity; host-local static service tokens are not the baseline.
Firmware changes on A should be policy-gated maintenance operations with cohort-aware preflight rather than ambient background updater behavior.
Fleet host updates on A stay health-gated and rollout-shaped: signed channels are byte authority, while cohorts/windows/assignments and reboot coordination stay policy-derived and receipted.
Fleet install/recovery should bind to target-device identity and keep destructive disk mutation in breakglass/maintenance policy rather than routine automation.
High-risk shared-trust mutations on A should require digest-bound approvals from distinct principals; requester-self-approval and “approve the idea” workflows are not the fleet default.

Kernel mutation on A should stay activation-first: boot tunables live in the generation, runtime sysctl writes outside activation require maintenance leases, and kmods are preload-first rather than ambient runtime tools.

Fleet device authority should stay compiled-minimal and lease-expanded: raw block, packet-capture, USB, HID, and similar high-authority nodes are maintenance-shaped rather than ambient service authority.
Fleet evidence on A should stay always-on but bounded: local journal/diagnostics/flight-recorder capture is normal, while richer export or retention changes remain policy- and receipt-shaped.
Fleet networking on A should stay activation-first and policy-derived: risky host topology edits use maintenance leases and commit-confirmed rollback rather than shell folklore.
Fleet trust roots should stay purpose-scoped and diff-gated; official lanes block embedded shadow trust unless an explicit waiver says otherwise.
Destructive wipe/reseed on A should stay target-bound and digest-bound, with breakglass or maintenance authority rather than ambient reinstall toggles.
Fleet GC should preserve a hard bootable rollback floor; aggressive reclamation belongs in dry-run-first policy-approved plans rather than disk-pressure panic cleanup.
Fleet fuzz posture on A keys on shipped trusted-plane uapi/parser/driver target classes and zero open reproducible cases for those classes before normal promotion.

notes: Host runs trusted UI, portals, mediation, update, and recovery tooling; general interactive apps are AppVM-first.
